title: A hidden neighborhood
question: Who lives where the oxygen runs out?
intervention: Watch the Oxygen overlay (Lab → Observe) while the lid stays closed. Tap a Sprinter and a Dusk and read what holds each one back. Look for one held back by too little oxygen and the other by too much; if the inspector names something else, note what holds them back instead.
predictedTradeoff: Sprinters burn oxygen to eat, so a busy patch under a closed lid can run short of it for them. Dusks are held back where oxygen is high; if the Sprinters use up enough oxygen, that may leave room for Dusks.
confounds: Both species eat the same sugar, so they compete for food as well as being sorted by oxygen. The time limited by oxygen counts every organism each tenth of a second, so a bigger group adds up faster. One run with one seed.

all.label: Sprinters were held back by too little oxygen
Dusks were held back by too much oxygen

completion.journalStamp: Measured Sprinters short of oxygen and Dusks held back by it
